title: Message
description: Lightweight global feedback shown at the edge of the screen, called imperatively from anywhere.

types.title: Types
types.description: message.success / error / info / warning / loading accept a string or any React node.

options.title: Options
options.description: Pass an options object to set the duration, close button, icon, progress bar, hover behavior and more. message.config({ maxCount }) limits how many messages are shown at once.

placements.title: Placements
placements.description: Six screen positions; messages at the same position are stacked.

update.title: Update a message
update.description: Keep the returned id and call message.update to change the content, type or duration.

use-message.title: useMessage
use-message.description: The hook returns promise-based methods that resolve when the message closes, so steps can be chained with await.

destroy.title: Close programmatically
destroy.description: message.destroy(id) closes one message; message.destroy() closes all of them.

MessageProps.id: Unique id; generated automatically when omitted in MessageOptions. Reusing the id of an open message replaces it
MessageProps.type: Message type, which sets the color. Set by the method you call (message.success, ...)
MessageProps.duration: Time in milliseconds before the message closes automatically; 0 keeps it open. Defaults to message.config().duration
MessageProps.onClose: Called with the message id when the message closes, whatever the reason
MessageProps.showProgress: Shows a countdown progress bar (only when duration > 0)
MessageProps.pauseOnHover: Pauses the countdown and progress bar while hovered or while keyboard focus is inside the message
MessageProps.placement: Screen position of the message stack. Defaults to message.config().placement
MessageProps.onClick: Called when the message content is activated; the content then renders as a keyboard operable button
MessageProps.description: Extra description exposed to assistive technologies (aria-description)
MessageProps.closeAriaLabel: Accessible label of the close button
MessageProps.onUpdate: Called after message.update() re-renders the message

imperative.title: Imperative API
imperative.intro: Messages are not rendered as JSX. Call the global message object, or the useMessage hook inside components, and pass either the content or a MessageOptions object (MessageProps with an optional id).

rows.show: Shows a message of the given type and returns its id. A plain string or React element is used as content; an object with a content key is treated as options.
rows.update: Merges new props into an open message and re-renders it, e.g. turning a loading message into a success. Unknown ids are ignored.
rows.destroy: Closes the message with the given id, or every open message when called without an id. onClose is called for each closed message.
rows.hook: Returns a stable object of promise-based methods for use inside components.
rows.hookShow: Shows a message and returns a promise that resolves when it closes. The promise also exposes the message id as messageId.
rows.hookManage: The same functions as message.update and message.destroy.
rows.options: Options accepted by every show method: all MessageProps except that id is optional.
rows.promise: Return value of the useMessage show methods.
rows.config: Sets global defaults (duration, placement, maxCount) for messages created afterwards; when maxCount is exceeded the oldest messages close. Call without arguments to restore the built-in defaults.
rows.configType: Options of message.config(). Defaults: duration 3000, placement "topRight", maxCount unlimited.

notes.title: Notes
notes.id: Pass your own id to update or close a message later; otherwise use the returned id (message-0, message-1, …).
notes.onClose: onClose is called exactly once per message, whether it closes on timeout, through the close button or through destroy.
notes.stacking: Each placement has its own stack container appended to document.body; it is removed when its last message closes.
notes.promise: To chain messages, await the promise or return only messageId from then(): returning the result itself would also wait for the next message to close.
notes.a11y: Errors and warnings use role="alert" (announced immediately); other types use role="status" (announced politely). With pauseOnHover, the countdown also pauses while keyboard focus is inside a message, so the close button can be reached in time.
